selection.candidates: all COMPLETE trials of the model's study (target 200)
selection.primary: min KL s.t. refusals <= 10/100 (ties: fewer refusals, then lower trial number)
selection.fallback1: min refusals s.t. KL <= 1.0 (ties: lower KL, then lower trial number)
selection.fallback2: Pareto point minimising sqrt((ref/100)^2 + KL^2) (ties: lower trial number)
selection.export: Heretic's own save menu (export path 1), LoRA adapter only (4-bit merge needs ~48GB CPU RAM)
selection.provisional: if a study has <200 complete trials the same rule is applied and the selection is labelled PROVISIONAL

a3.units: the 60 TPE startup edits (trials 0-59), identical parameter draws across the two models (seed 20260923); one seed; EN only

readings.shared surface: rho_ref >= 0.9 AND rho_kl >= 0.9, both lower bootstrap CI >= 0.8, AND dR2_sibling > 0.05 with bootstrap CI > 0 (both outcomes)
readings.shared via strength only: raw rho >= 0.9 but dR2_sibling CI includes 0

kl_matched_subset.criterion: |log KL_gams - log KL_gemma| <= its median over the shared edits

efficiency.interpretation_limits: Two models are two units: this quantifies a difference between THESE two checkpoints under THESE conditions (bnb_4bit NF4, one optimizer seed, English keyword refusal scoring, 4-bit dequantized edits). It does not attribute the difference to Slovene continued pretraining, to instruction tuning or to any particular training stage - GaMS3-12B-Instruct is a same-family reference, not a controlled derivative of this Gemma checkpoint. The published bf16 Heretic edit of gemma-3-12b-it reaches 3/100 refusals with 200 trials, so the Gemma arm's resistance here is confounded with quantization and with the reduced trial budget and must not be read as 'gemma-3-12b-it cannot be abliterated'.
